interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines link PI-RADS scores to PSA density categories to guide biopsy decisions. "linking PI-RADS score (1-2, 3, and 4-5) to PSA-D categories (< 0.10, 0.10-0.15, 0.15-0.20 and > 0.20ng/mL) (Table 5.5) [230]. This risk-adapted matrix table may guide the decision to perform a biopsy." For this patient, the PI-RADS score is 4 and the PSA density is 0.296 ng/mL².

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
Expert 1's suggestion of biopsy is based on numerous panel variables, but the guideline suggests that the risk-adapted matrix table is the primary tool. The guideline makes decisive that no single panel variable represents the decision when a risk-adapted matrix is available. The precedent cited by Expert 5 shows that the decision in similar cases varied based on the specific PI-RADS score and PSA level, which is a fact the guideline makes decisive that no panel variable represents.

WHAT WE STILL NEED
The panel already contains the PI-RADS score of 4 and the PSA density of 0.296 ng/mL². The guideline suggests that the risk-adapted matrix table may guide the decision. The panel does not contain the specific PSA-D cut-off values from Table 5.5, which is required to apply the matrix. The panel does not contain the specific ISUP grade thresholds mentioned in the guideline. The panel does not contain the specific information regarding the prior biopsy outcome or the specific PSA trend beyond the velocity.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 9.30 ng/mL over 4 points spanning 31 months; velocity +0.94 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 67 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 14.6 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 4.2-50.8.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

  uncertainty  +/- 0.05 epistemic (95% band 0.71-0.93), of which 0.00 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 89% of the time over the 37 labelled cases in this tier

interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents opened by the registrar—the radiology report, PSA trend, and previous notes—directly address the variables weighed by the trace model and the questions posed by the moderator, except for the specific PSA-D cut-off values and family history, which were not explicitly requested as answers to the open questions.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved evidence strongly aligns with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's answer of BIOPSY, as the cohort criterion (PI-RADS $\ge 3$) fired, and the registrar confirmed "None" for prior biopsy history.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. What is the specific ISUP grade threshold mentioned in the EAU guideline that should be used for the csPCa probability? This specific threshold was not retrieved by the registrar.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS score of 4, which triggered the cohort criterion, is the most decisive factor here, as it is explicitly weighted as "decisive" in the panel protocol. The PSA trend showing a drop from 6.7 to 9.3 ng/mL supports the need for action.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
Given the strong alignment of the cohort criterion and the high predicted cancer probability, I suggest proceeding with a biopsy. The decision is ready based on the retrieved evidence, pending the application of the missing guideline parameters.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
